claim: Code-MUE (ISSTA 2026) is a purely black-box uncertainty framework that clusters sampled code generations into a Semantic Interaction Graph via observed runtime execution behavior and computes the Von Neumann entropy of that graph as a whole-solution uncertainty score, achieving Spearman correlation up to -0.98 with functional correctness across 8 SOTA code LLMs.
stance_target: efficacy of execution-grounded (vs. purely lexical) uncertainty signals for code correctness
scope_conditions: 8 state-of-the-art code LLMs, black-box setting (applicable to closed-source models)
quoted_support: A large-scale empirical study across eight state-of-the-art LLMs demonstrates that Code-MUE achieves a strong negative correlation with functional correctness (Spearman's correlation up to -0.98), significantly outperforming lexical and embedding-based baselines

claim: Code-MUE demonstrates measured downstream utility of execution-grounded uncertainty in two practical workflows: selective prediction/risk detection (abstaining on risky generations) and response selection/re-ranking among sampled candidates.
stance_target: downstream utility of code-generation confidence signals (directive: does confidence enable a measured downstream win)
scope_conditions: whole-solution granularity, selective prediction and re-ranking workflows
quoted_support: significantly outperforming lexical and embedding-based baselines while enabling robust risk detection and selective prediction in practical workflows

claim: Code-MUE's uncertainty is a whole-solution scalar (one entropy value per generation/problem), not a per-requirement or per-test-case decomposition, so it cannot localize which specific requirement a solution is likely to fail -- it is a same-granularity competitor to DPRC's scalar oracle baseline, not to DPRC's per-method result.
stance_target: DPRC's differentiation on granularity and the identification of an open downstream-utility gap at the per-requirement level
scope_conditions: comparison of Code-MUE granularity vs DPRC per-method granularity
quoted_support: Code-MUE's uncertainty is a WHOLE-SOLUTION scalar (one entropy value per generation/problem) derived from black-box execution clustering across samples -- it does not decompose into per-requirement/per-test-case confidence
